principles: Public sources only. Nothing confidential, internal or personal is collected.
Original sources are preferred: the organisation that did the work or holds the evidence. A third-party report is used only when no original can be found, and is labelled as such.
UK government sources are checked first, then AI developers' own threat and safety reporting, then independent evaluators.

Anything not from UK government or a frontier AI developer must pass the inclusion test: a real AI-enabled attack or AI security incident; health and care or the wider public sector; action on AI cyber risk the UK or NHS is likely to follow; or a change in what attackers can do or access.

changes.change: Source rules tightened. Core is now limited to UK government departments and public bodies with an AI or cyber security remit, frontier AI developers, and leading research bodies whose work AISI, NCSC or a frontier developer has cited. Other organisations with 2 or more News items in 90 days become hints. Existing core organisations re-checked against the new test: all qualify (MI5, Cabinet Office and MHRA under 1(i); Carnegie Mellon under 1(iii), as ExploitBench is cited by AISI).
changes.why: Keep core strict; volume alone should not make an organisation core.

changes.change: Added MI5 AI Threat Assessment Centre to core sources
changes.why: Rule 1(i): a UK government body set up in October 2026 to produce all-source assessments of AI national security threats.

changes.change: Added Cabinet Office to core sources
changes.why: Rule 1(ii): it published 3 News items in the last 90 days (PM's AI Taskforce on 24 July, the Minister for AI speech on 12 October and the UK-Canada AI security partnership on 13 October).

changes.change: Added MHRA to core sources and removed the MHRA AI as a medical device reforms hint
changes.why: Rule 1(ii): it published 3 News items in the last 90 days (National Commission recommendations on 10 September, the government response on 6 October and the MHRA 2030 Strategy on 14 October).

changes.change: Added Carnegie Mellon (ExploitBench) to core sources
changes.why: Rule 1(ii): it is the publisher of 5 ExploitBench result items in the last 90 days (4 September and 24 September 2026).

changes.change: Core and hint lists are now kept by fixed rules: promote to core a UK government body or national AI safety or security institute with an AI security remit, or any organisation with 3 or more News items in 90 days; move a core organisation to hints after 180 days with nothing relevant. AISI, NCSC and the CSR Bill are fixed.
changes.why: Make source coverage decisions objective and auditable rather than case by case.

changes.change: Core sources are now organisations checked across their whole website for AI and cyber material. Added Anthropic's research page and OpenAI's misalignment reports page to the pages checked.
changes.why: Four cyber-relevant Anthropic posts appeared only on its research page and were missed; John wants every core organisation covered thoroughly.

changes.change: Added a written inclusion test for stories from outside UK government and the frontier AI developers, and a Wider AI news tab for significant AI news with no cyber angle. Three items moved there from News.
changes.why: Make inclusion criteria explicit and auditable, and keep significant non-cyber AI news visible without diluting the cyber dataset.
